A little spoonful for daddy, one for mommy.
I beg your pardon. Could you make me some tea?
Right, eat! Eat and don't hold us up.

Marinochka, please put the spoon down. I'll feed him myself.

Well, not so fast! — I say, eat!
Do you understand that you've made us sick of you already?
Eduard Valentinovich! Why are you so nervous?
Are you afraid that the little pill will stop working?
How? And how did you find out about the little pill?
So you were eavesdropping in there, yes? — Yes, I was eavesdropping.

What have you done? — Marina, he's lying, he's a faker!
He poured this porridge on his head himself! His arms are healthy!
Get out of here! — Alright, calm down, he's gone.

действовать.gloss: to act, to take action; to work

meanings.en: to act, to take action, to get to work

meanings.en: to work, to be in effect
meanings.note: правило действует = the rule is in force

examples.text: В детстве я жил в Москве.

examples.trans: My childhood was hard. I grew up in a communal flat.

достать.gloss: to take out, to get, to reach

meanings.en: to take out, to pull out, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

meanings.en: to get hold of, to obtain

examples.trans: And take his eye out with a spoon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.
